gloss: microphone (the full form of the common abbreviation マイク)

definitions.gloss: microphone — an instrument that converts sound into an electrical signal for amplification, recording, or transmission
definitions.explanation: An electroacoustic device that converts sound into an electrical signal. マイクロフォン is the full-length transliteration of English "microphone," but in everyday Japanese the abbreviation マイク is overwhelmingly more common. The full form is reserved for formal, technical, or product-specification contexts — audio-equipment specs, academic discussion, broadcasting technical vocabulary, and brand or model names.

examples.japanese: {高性能|こうせいのう}のマイクロフォン。
{歌|うた}を{録音|ろくおん}するためにマイクロフォンを{用意|ようい}した。
examples.english: I prepared a microphone in order to record a song.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}{室|しつ}には{天井|てんじょう}{埋|う}め{込|こ}み{型|がた}のマイクロフォンが{設置|せっち}されている。
examples.english: Ceiling-mounted microphones are installed in the conference room.

examples.japanese: プロ{用|よう}のコンデンサーマイクロフォンは、{細|こま}やかな{音|おと}の{違|ちが}いまで{忠実|ちゅうじつ}に{捉|とら}えることができる。
examples.english: Professional condenser microphones can faithfully capture even subtle differences in sound.

notes:
マイクロフォン is the full-length loanword for "microphone." In everyday speech, the abbreviation マイク is dominant; the full form is mostly limited to formal, technical, and product-specification contexts.

ABBREVIATION:
- The everyday word is マイク. Carrying a microphone at a karaoke session, a wedding, or a presentation, a Japanese speaker would say マイク almost without exception.
- マイクロフォン is used in: audio-equipment specs ({指向性|しこうせい}マイクロフォン "directional microphone"), academic discussion (acoustics, communications engineering), product names and packaging, and broadcasting/recording-industry contexts.

TYPES (often in compound form):
- ダイナミックマイクロフォン: dynamic microphone — durable, common in live sound
- コンデンサーマイクロフォン: condenser microphone — sensitive, common in studios
- ピンマイクロフォン: lavalier/pin microphone — clipped to clothing
- ワイヤレスマイクロフォン: wireless microphone
- {指向性|しこうせい}マイクロフォン: directional microphone
- {無指向性|むしこうせい}マイクロフォン: omnidirectional microphone

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マイクロフォンを{使|つか}う: to use a microphone
- マイクロフォンに{向|む}かって{話|はな}す: to speak into the microphone
- マイクロフォンを{設置|せっち}する: to set up a microphone
- {高性能|こうせいのう}マイクロフォン: high-performance microphone
- マイクロフォン{入力|にゅうりょく}: microphone input (an audio jack/port)

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- マイク: the standard everyday abbreviation; what speakers actually say in daily life
- スピーカー: speaker (audio output) — the reverse device, converting electrical signal to sound
- ヘッドセット: headset — a combined microphone and headphones unit
- ヘッドホン: headphones
- {音声|おんせい}{入力|にゅうりょく}: audio/voice input — broader; refers to the input signal rather than the device
- レコーディング: recording

USAGE NOTES:
- In casual speech, always prefer マイク. Saying マイクロフォン in everyday conversation sounds slightly stiff or overly precise.
- The katakana spelling has a small ォ as part of フォ (representing the "fo" sound). Older spellings sometimes used マイクロホン (with ホ instead of フォ), but フォ is now standard.
- Note that マイク by itself can occasionally cause ambiguity with proper names like "Mike" (the English given name), but context usually disambiguates.
